newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Olive oil reform plans set for back burner.
newsitem.headline: Olive oil reform plans set for back burner.

text.p: Farm ministers are expected on Tuesday to confirm deep disagreement over olive oil reform plans which are as a result likely to be delayed, EU officials and diplomats said.
They said that producing countries are set to renew a strong attack at next week's Farm Council on a reform option linking subsidies to the number of productive trees.

Spain, backed by Portugal, Greece and Italy, would prefer a second option that would retain the production-based subsidy system but would scrap special aid for small producers, seen as the main source of fraud.
Both options were presented by the European Commission in a report in February noting that olive oil fraud was proportionately 10 times greater than for cereals and other crops.
Little progress has been made since farm ministers discussed the report in April, diplomats said, adding that a working group has confirmed deep disagreement over market trends.
The Commission, supported by consumers, predicts a growing surplus as a result of increasing production and stagnant consumption and exports.
Producers say that the prediction is based on figures for the last two years which are unrepresentative and that greater effort should be made to boost consumption.
They argue that fundamental reforms are unnecessary.
With the European Parliament only expected to give its opinion on olive oil reform in the autumn, the Commission is under no time pressure to draft reform proposals, diplomats noted.
